doctor: NAME_1, how long already the cough?
patient: Three days doctor, malam lagi teruk. Ada kahak kuning.
doctor: Any chest pain or breathless?
patient: No chest pain. Sikit-sikit breathless when climb stairs only.
doctor: Temperature 37.9, pulse 92, oxygen 97 percent. Throat red, chest clear. This is viral upper respiratory infection. Paracetamol 1 gram four times a day if fever. Review in one week, come earlier if breathless worsen or fever not settle. I order FBC if not improving.
output:
Title: Productive cough with mild dyspnea  

## Subjective  
- Cough present for three days, worse at nighttime  
- Yellow sputum noted  
- Mild shortness of breath during stair climbingonly  
- No chest pain reported  

## Objective  
- Temperature 37.9°C  
- Pulse rate 92 beats per minute  
- Oxygen saturation 97% on room air  
- Throat reddened, chest examination clear  

## Assessment  
- Viral upper respiratory tract infection with productive cough  

## Plan  
- Paracetamol 1 g every 8 hours as needed for fever  
- Monitor for worsening breathing or persistent fever  

## Orders & follow-ups  
- Repeat full blood count (FBC) if condition does not improve  
- Follow up in seven days unless signs of deterioration occur  
- Seek early return if breathlessness increases or fever persists beyond expected resolution time

doctor: NAME_1 what brings you in?
patient: Itchy rash on both arms since yesterday, doctor. Very itchy at night.
doctor: Any new soaps, foods, medicines?
patient: I used a new detergent two days ago.
doctor: Rash looks like contact dermatitis. Stop the detergent. Cetirizine 10 milligram at night for five days. Come back if it spreads or blisters.
output:
Title: Itchy rash following detergent use  

## Subjective  
- Itchy rash appeared on both arms overnight  
- Symptoms worsen significantly at nighttime  
- New detergent introduced two days prior to onset  

## Objective  
- Rash consistent with contact dermatitis appearance  
- No blister formation observed  
- No associated fever or systemic signs mentioned  

## Assessment  
- Contact dermatitis secondary to new detergent exposure  

## Plan  
- Discontinue use of current detergent immediately  
- Initiate cetirizine 10 mg nightly for five days  

## Orders & follow-ups  
- Avoid further skin exposure to suspected irritant  
- Return visit required if rash expands or forms blisters  
- Monitor for development of additional lesions or worsening itch intensity

patient: Morning readings around seven. But my knee pain worse two weeks already, I take ibuprofen sometimes.
doctor: Careful with ibuprofen, your gastritis history. Fasting glucose 6.8 today, blood pressure 128 over 82, weight stable. Continue metformin 500 milligram twice daily. For the knee use topical diclofenac gel three times daily instead of ibuprofen. HbA1c test today, physio referral for the knee. Review in three months with results.
output:
Title: Diabetes management with worsening knee pain  

## Subjective  
- Morning blood sugar readings approximately seven  
- Knee pain has worsened over the past two weeks  
- Occasionally uses ibuprofen for pain Relief  

## Objective  
- Fasting glucose level 6.8 mmol/L  
- Blood pressure 128/82 mmHg  
- Weight unchanged  

## Assessment  
- Stable glycemic control currently  
- Chronic gastritis history prompting caution with NSAIDs  
- Persistent knee pain requiring alternative analgesic approach  

## Plan  
- Continue metformin 500 mg orally twice daily  
- Switch to topical diclofenac gel applied three times daily for knee pain  
- Avoid oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs due to gastric risk  

## Orders & follow-ups  
- Repeat HbA1c testing scheduled today  
- Referral made to physical therapy for knee condition  
- Scheduled clinic review in three months pending lab results
